I remember when I was in school, having rules helped me understand what was acceptable behavior and what wasn't. It gave me a sense of structure. Also, the scenario mentions that Mr. Smith had "no control" over the children. That suggests that without rules, he couldn't manage the class effectively. Furthermore, rules aren't just about punishment; they're about setting expectations and helping students understand how to behave in a way that's conducive to learning. When students know the rules, they can focus more on their studies rather than worrying about what's allowed or not. It creates a sense of security and predictability.
